source.caption: Atlas text (printed p. 47): 'Fig. 3.35. Al2O3-SiO2 phase diagram with incongruent melting of mullite (3Al2O3·2SiO2) according to Klug et al. [1] (full lines - recommended version of the phase diagram), Aksay, Pask [2] (dash-dot lines), and Shindo [3] (dashed lines). The version by Klug et al. [1] is also based on the previous results reported by Aramaki, Roy [4], Aksay, Pask [1] and Horibe, Kuwabara [5]. Earlier versions of the phase diagram with incongruent melting of mullite have been reported by Bowen, Greig [6], Shears, Archibald [7], Trömel et al. [8] and Welch [9]. As reported by Welch [9], Horibe, Kuwabara [5] and Shindo [3], the composition of liquid co-existing with mullite and Al2O3, in contrast to the phase diagram reported by Aksay, Pask [2], is rather close to the mullite composition.' References: [1] Klug, F. J., S. Prochazka, R. H. Doremus: J. Am. Ceram. Soc. 70 (1987) No. 10, p. 750/9; [2] Aksay, I. A., J. A. Pask: Science 183 (1973) No. 4120, p. 69/71; [3] Shindo, I.: Ceram. Trans. 6 /Mullite Mullite Matrix Compos./ (1990), p. 103/13; [4] Aramaki, S., S. Roy: J. Am. Ceram. Soc. 45 (1962) No. 5, p. 229/42; [5] Horibe, T., S. Kuwabara: Bull. Chem. Soc. Jap. 40 (1967) No. 4, p. 972/82; [6] Bowen, N. L., J. W. Greig: J. Am. Ceram. Soc. 7 (1924) No. 4, p. 238/54; [7] Shears, E. C., W. A. Archibald: Iron Steel 27 (1954) No. 2, p. 61/6; [8] Trömel, G., K.-H. Obst, K. Konopicky, H. Bauer, I. Patzak: Ber. Dtsch. Keram. Ges. 34 (1957) No. 12, p. 397/402; [9] Welch, J. W.: Nature 186 (1960) No. 4724, p. 546/7.

invariants.notes: Incongruent melting of mullite (Klug et al.): mullite → corundum + liquid. Temperature and composition not printed. Liquid composition close to mullite, as the caption states. NSRDS-NBS 61 lists eutectics only, no cross-check possible.
Temperature and composition not printed. NBS 5909 (1547 °C, approximate) disagrees and is not attached (`unmatchedSourcePoints`).

variantChoice.reason: Atlas text: Fig. 3.35 full lines are the 'recommended version'; Fig. 3.36 caption: the version with incongruent melting 'represents the stable phase relations', the congruent version 'the metastable phase relations'. Consistent with Fig. 3.166.
